cim: Pennsylvania Requires Disclosures For Ads Whose Synthetic Content Creates False Consumer Perceptions
cim_eredeti: Pennsylvania Requires Disclosures For Ads Whose Synthetic Content Creates False Consumer Perceptions
szoveg_eredeti:
Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed the Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Advertising Act (Act 99 of 2026) into law on October 22, 2026. Effective December 21, 2026, the Act prohibits an advertiser from creating and disseminating or causing the creation and dissemination of an advertisement that uses “synthetic content” in a manner that creates a “false consumer perception” about the nature, origin, or authenticity of the advertised goods or services, unless the advertisement clearly and conspicuously discloses that it contains content that was modified or generated using artificial intelligence.

Pennsylvania joins New York, whose synthetic performer disclosure requirement took effect June 9, 2026, and California, whose law takes effect January 1, 2027. Those laws reach only “synthetic performers”—digital performers that do not depict an identifiable person. Pennsylvania’s law is broader in that it extends to any AI-generated or significantly AI-modified content, but narrower in that it only applies where that content creates a false consumer perception. And unlike New York’s law, which requires actual knowledge, the Act imposes no knowledge or intent requirement.

The false consumer perception trigger drew criticism in the Senate floor debate, where Senator Jarrett Coleman, who opposed the bill, argued that advertising has always used “enhancement” through “professional lighting, idealized staging, [and] models in perfect conditions,” and the standard does not provide “meaningful guidance” on where enhancement ends and deception begins.
